indicator_definition: The NEET rate measures the proportion of young people aged 15 to 29 who are not in employment, education or training, expressed as a percentage of the total population in that age group. It identifies young people at risk of labour market exclusion and social marginalisation. Data are based on the EU Labour Force Survey.
rationale: Young people who are NEET face long-term risks to their employment prospects, earnings and social integration. Reducing the NEET rate requires investment in education, vocational training and active labour market policies. Progress means a sustained reduction in the proportion of young people outside employment, education and training.
methodology_characteristics: Data are collected through the EU Labour Force Survey (EU-LFS). NEET status combines information on employment status and participation in education or training in the four weeks preceding the survey. Data are published annually.
indicator_name: Young people neither in employment nor in education or training (NEET)
